messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — GPU pool 'gpu-prod-usw' reporting sustained queue growth. Pending queue > 500, tail latency > 4s, autoscaler attempted multiple scale actions but failed. Root cause unknown, triggering on-call.

pagerbot: Severity: P2. Affected service: hosted-inference (text-generation, embeddings). Pager sent to oncall rotation.

mia: ack, I’m on it. I see 500+ pending requests on the queue metrics, and a spike of 502/503s from the runtime. Routing is starting to fallback to lower-tier nodes.

ash: noted. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures when creating instances: `Error: quota.limit_exceeded` and intermittent 429s from cloud provider. Also a few API errors: `max_instances_reached`.

ash: additionally, driver logs on gpu-node-17..20 show repeated CUDA/Xid entries:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU Hang
[ 1234.568000] nvidia-smi: process 4321 (inference) was terminated due to GPU hang
```

samir: that Xid 79 pattern usually means the driver hung under heavy allocation pressure. We might be losing effective GPUs even though nodes are nominally up.

kevin: autoscaler attempted to add 50 nodes at 12:02 UTC, then 12:03 UTC saw errors like: `CreateInstance failed: Insufficient GPUs in quota` and `RateLimitExceeded`. Cloud ticket opened: TKT-4219.

jess: customer impact: several freemium customers reported 5xx on embeddings. Internal SLO for embeddings route breached. CS notified a small set of customers (list sent). Triage: short-term mitigation to avoid broader customer impact.

mia: immediate plan: 1) shift traffic on high-volume routes to fallback_model_small with 10% sampling to preserve quality but cut GPU load; 2) cordon nodes with repeated Xid and drain pods; 3) manual scale of Dedicated pools (if we have reserved spare capacity) and move high-paying customers there; 4) ask infra to temporary raise GPU quota/pools. Executing now.

mia: running commands:
```
kubectl get pods -l app=inference -n prod -o wide
kubectl cordon gpu-node-18 && kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod
# switching route split
redwoodctl routes set-split /v1/generate fallback_model_small=0.1 primary=0.9 --force
```

ash: cordoned gpu-node-18 and gpu-node-19; draining 18 shows multiple evictions due to OOM on driver-managed processes. Reprovision in progress.

samir: seeing memory pressure patterns in dmesg on those nodes:
```
[ 9876.4321] Out of memory: Kill process 5432 (inference) score 987 or sacrifice child
[ 9876.4322] nvidia-nvlink: memory allocator returned -12
```

kevin: contacted cloud quota team. They can grant a temporary bump of 30 GPUs in us-west for 2 hours; need approval from finance. Request submitted, ETA ~25m. Meanwhile autoscaler still failing due to provider 429s.

jess: rolling traffic for the two largest paying customers to Dedicated hosts now to avoid errors. Notifying them via CS.

infra-bot: Autoscaler debug snippet: `ScaleOp: desired=170 -> attempted=220 -> failed_create=50: [quota.limit_exceeded, rate_limit]`

mia: driver hotpatch/rollback: we see nodes on driver version 515.* and 510.*. rolling back 515.x to 510.85 on affected nodes as a precaution (there's a known instability with 515 under sustained kernel RO). Coordinating with eng-runtime.

ash: rolling rollback started on nodes 17-20. Will reboot after driver change.

eng-oncall: note — before rebooting, remove any long-lived KV caches to avoid bad state restore. Command: `redis-cli -h cache-prod flushdb some-prefix` (we will be surgical).

samir: after cordon + driver rollback + manual reprovision, queue depth dropped to ~120 and 2xx rate improved from 78% -> 92% on main generation route. Still seeing intermittent regressions.

mia: monitoring: I'm keeping the fallback route active at 10% and the dedicated migrations for 2h. If cloud quota bump arrives we scale further otherwise we'll keep conservative traffic shaping.

kevin: cloud quota bumped +30 GPUs applied at 12:48 UTC (TKT-4219 resolved). Autoscaler re-attempt queued actions and managed to create 20 nodes before hitting provider rate lim again; creation throttle means we ramp slowly.

ash: created nodes are healthy but two instances hit Xid 79 shortly after join — suspect persistent kernel/driver interaction. Those nodes are quarantined and will be reprovisioned with rollback driver.

jess: customer update sent: short blurb to impacted customers, apology + mitigation steps + ETA to restore normal latency.

mia: current status — queue depth stable ~90, error rate back under SLO for majority of customers but embeddings still slightly elevated. I'll keep this marked active and do a handoff to oncall for a 2h watch. We'll post a preliminary postmortem later with timeline and action items: increase autoscaler backoff jitter, add quota runway alerts, validate driver compatibility matrix, add a reactive fallback policy for model routes.

eng-oncall: handing off to next oncall at 14:00 UTC. Please include runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-capacity and add logs to incident ticket INC-7892.

pagerbot: Incident acknowledged. Severity remains P2. Handoff complete.

mia: final note — root appears to be combined: provider quota + autoscaler throttling -> slow scale -> queue growth -> driver stress on older nodes -> Xid/OOM reducing effective capacity. Mitigations: traffic fallback, cordon/reboot with rollback, temporary quota bump, customer migrations. Will follow up with RCA draft. :thumbsup:
